questions.question: Who among the following was the first Law and Justice Minister of independent India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**BR Ambedkar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **BR Ambedkar** was the first Law and Justice Minister of independent India.
 
• He served as the Chairman of the Drafting Committee for the Indian Constitution.
 
• Ambedkar played a crucial role in framing the laws and policies for the newly independent nation.
 
• He was a key architect in establishing the legal and social framework of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Law and Justice Ministry**:

 
 
• The Ministry is responsible for the administration of justice, legal reforms, and legal advice to the Government of India.
 
• It oversees the functioning of the legal and judicial system in the country.
 
 
 
• **Indian Constitution**:
 
 
• The Constitution of India was adopted on 26 January 1950.
 
• It is the supreme law of India and provides the framework for the political principles, procedures, and powers of government institutions.
 
 
 
• **Drafting Committee**:
 
 
• The Drafting Committee was formed on 29 August 1947 to draft the Constitution of India.
 
• BR Ambedkar was appointed as the Chairman of this committee.
 
 
 
• **Social Reforms**:
 
 
• Ambedkar was a prominent social reformer and fought against social discrimination and the caste system.
 
• He played a significant role in uplifting the downtrodden and marginalized sections of society.

questions.question: Who among the following addressed the Indian National congress as its President in 1887?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Badruddin Tyabji.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the British Raj, Badruddin Tyabji (10 October 1844 – 19 August 1906) was an Indian lawyer, activist, and politician.
 
• The first Indian to work as a barrister in the High Court of Bombay was Tyabji.
 
• In 1887, he held the position of Indian National Congress' third president.
 
• He served as the first Muslim president of the Indian National Congress and was one of its founding members.
 
• In 1874, he established the Anjuman-i-Islam College in Bombay.
 
• Tyabji also campaigned to undermine the zenana system and for the freedom of women.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Gopal Krishna Gokhale (9 May 1866 – 19 February 1915):

 
 
• He was a social reformer and "moderate" political figure in India during the struggle for independence.
 
• Gokhale was the founder of the Servants of India Society.
 
• He was a prominent member of the Indian National Congress.
 
 
 
• Dadabhai Naoroji (4 September 1825 – 30 June 1917):
 
 
• He was an author, businessman, scholar, and political figure in India.
 
• He presided over the Indian National Congress from 1886 to 1887, 1893 to 1894, and 1906 to 1907 as its second, ninth, and 22nd president.
 
 
 
• Surendranath Banerjee (10 November 1848 – 6 August 1925):
 
 
• He led the Indian nationalist movement under British rule.
 
• He established the Indian National Association, a nationalist group.
 
• He was one of the Indian National Congress' founding members. 
 
 
 
• Womesh Chandra Bonerjee **(****29 December 1844-21 July 1906)**
 
 
• ​Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee was born on 29 December 1844 in **Calcutta**.
 
• In **1883 **he defended** Surendranath Banerjee **in the famous Contempt of Court Case against him in the** Calcutta High Court**.
 
• He presided over the **first **session of the Indian National Congress held at **Bombay **in **1885**.

questions.question: The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bombay**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Indian National Congress was founded and its first session was held in Bombay in 1885.
 
• W.C. Banerjee was its first president.
 
• It was attended by delegates from all over India. Persons attending the session belonged to different religious faiths.
 
• They discussed the problems of all the Indians irrespective of their religion, caste, language and region.
 
• The first session of the INC was proposed at Pune, but because of an outbreak of plague in Pune, the venue was shifted to Bombay.
 
• The first session was held in Bombay, at the Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit Pathshala.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• In the first session that was held at Bombay, there were a few important segments of the demands from Indians that were presented before the British. They are as under:

 
 
• ​Appointment of a commission to enquire into the working of the Indian Administration.
 
• This commission was to assess Indian Administration from 1858- till date.
 
• India Council in London should be abolished.
 
• The creation of legislative councils.
 
• Reduction of Military Expenditure.
 
• Civil Services Reform.

questions.question: Which of the following Rebellion occurred between 1855-56?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Santhal rebellion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Santhal Rebellion (1855-56):** 

 
 
• This was a **native rebellion in present-day Bihar and Jharkhand, in eastern India against both the British colonial authority and the corrupt zamindari system by the Santhal people.** 
 
• It started in 1855 and the rebellion was brutally crushed by the **English East India Company by 1856.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kol Rebellion (1831-32):** The Kol Rebellion was a tribal revolt in the Chota Nagpur area in eastern India, now located in present-day Jharkhand and Odisha.
 
• **Ramosi Rebellion (1822-1825): **
 
 
• The Ramosi Peasant Force was an armed force formed by the Ramosi people of the Sahyadri mountain range in India in the late 1820s to revolt against the British East India Company.
 
• The rebellion started around **1822 and ended by 1825**.
 
 
 
• **Paika Rebellion (1817):**
 
 
• **The Paika Rebellion,** also called the Paika Bidroha, was an armed rebellion against **British East India Company rule in Odisha, in eastern India.**
 
• It took place in **1817,** earlier than the timeframe you specified.
 
• **The Paikas** were the **traditional landowning militia of Odisha and served as warriors. **

questions.question: Who among the following freedom fighters of India was assassinated?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __Mahatma Gandhi.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

 
• On 30th Jan 1948, Mahatma Gandhi was assassinated by Nathuram Godse in the year 1948.
 
• On this day, India observes Martyrs Day or Shaheed Diwas.
 
• It is observed to pay homage to **Mahatma Gandhi** and all **martyrs who sacrificed their life** for the **nation’s freedom**.
 
• He was born on 2 October 1869.
 
• Their political career Gandhi started in South Africa where he launched a Civil Disobedience Movement against the maltreatment meted out to Asian settlers.
 
• In 1915, he returned to India and took up the leadership of the National Freedom Struggle.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi led the national freedom struggle against British rule.
 
• Gandhiji launched many movements to force the British to concede India its Independence.
 
• The well-known are is Non-Co-operation Movement (1920), Civil Disobedience Movement

questions.question: Who had founded the first Women’s University in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dhondo Keshav Karve**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dhondo Keshav Karve** founded the first Women's University in India.
 
• The university is known as **SNDT Women's University (Shreemati Nathibai Damodar Thackersey Women's University)**.
 
• It was established in **1916** in Pune, Maharashtra.
 
• Dhondo Keshav Karve was a prominent social reformer and educator who dedicated his life to the cause of women's education and empowerment.
 
• He was awarded the **Bharat Ratna**, India's highest civilian award, in **1958** for his immense contributions to society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The establishment of SNDT Women's University marked a significant milestone in the history of women's education in India.
 
• The university initially started with just five students and has now grown to accommodate thousands of students across various disciplines.
 
• SNDT Women's University has several campuses and affiliated colleges spread across **Maharashtra **and other states.
 
• The university offers a wide range of undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral programs, catering to the educational needs of women from diverse backgrounds.
 
• Dhondo Keshav Karve's vision and efforts have had a lasting impact on the progress and empowerment of women in India.

questions.question: The autobiography, 'An Autobiography' by Jawaharlal Nehru is also known as ____________.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Toward Freedom**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Toward Freedom** is the alternate title for Jawaharlal Nehru's autobiography, originally written as **'An Autobiography'**.
 
• The book provides a detailed insight into **Nehru's political journey, personal life, and the freedom struggle of India.**
 
• It was written during Nehru's imprisonment between **1934 and 1935**.
 
• The autobiography highlights his thoughts on **Indian politics, socialism, nationalism, and his vision for India's future.**
 
• It also reflects his perspectives on global political movements and events during the early 20th century.
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru was the **first Prime Minister of India** and a key figure in the Indian independence movement.
 
• The book serves as an important historical document, offering insights into the mindset and philosophy of one of India's prominent leaders.
 
• Nehru's writing style is marked by **clarity, eloquence, and depth of thought.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **My Idea of Education**__

 __
 
• The title **'My Idea of Education'** is not related to Jawaharlal Nehru's autobiography.
 
• It may refer to other writings or works discussing education philosophies, but it is not connected to Nehru's work.
 
 
 
• **The Accidental Prime Minister**__
 __
 
• **'The Accidental Prime Minister'** is a book written by **Sanjaya Baru**, focusing on **Dr. Manmohan Singh's tenure** as India's Prime Minister.
 
• It is unrelated to Jawaharlal Nehru's autobiography.
 
 
 
• **The Unfinished Innings**__
 
 
• **'The Unfinished Innings'** is not associated with Jawaharlal Nehru.
 
• It could refer to other works or autobiographies, possibly from sports personalities or political figures.

questions.question: Who among the following Mughal emperors built Sheesh Mahal in Agra?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shah Jahan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shah Jahan**, whose name means** "King of the World" in Persian, was the fifth Mughal emperor, who ruled from 1628 to 1658.**
 
• Known for his patronage of the arts, **Shah Jahan commissioned many magnificent architectural projects during his reign, with the Sheesh Mahal in Agra being one of them.**
 
• Sheesh Mahal, also known as **"Glass Palace", is situated inside the Agra Fort. It's renowned for its intricate mirror work.**
 
• Shah Jahan is most famous for the construction of the** Taj Mahal, built in memory of his beloved wife, Mumtaz Mahal.**
 
• His architectural** style often involved white marble and precious stones, leading to some of the most beautiful and iconic structures in India.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Who led the Congress in the second round table conference held in London?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahatma Gandhi**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi** led the Congress delegation in the **second round table conference** held in **London**.
 
• The second round table conference took place from **7th September 1931 to 1st December 1931**.
 
• This conference aimed to discuss constitutional reforms in India and included representatives from various Indian political and social groups.
 
• **Gandhi represented the Indian National Congress and was the sole representative of the Congress at this conference**.
 
• The conference, however, did not result in any significant progress towards Indian self-rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **first round table conference** was held from **November 1930 to January 1931**, and the **third round table conference** was held from **November to December 1932**.
 
• The round table conferences were a series of peace conferences organized by the British Government to discuss constitutional reforms in India.
 
• The **Government of India Act 1935** was eventually passed, incorporating some of the discussions from these conferences.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi's participation in the second round table conference was significant as it marked his first and only visit to London after the start of the freedom struggle in India.
